# Postgres type mapping

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-types-doc.py from rowx._core.postgres.type_table(); do not edit by hand -->

This page is generated from the type table in `crates/rowx-postgres/src/types.rs`, the single source of truth for the
runtime codecs and for `rowx check`. Regenerate it with `uv run python scripts/gen-types-doc.py`.

- **Result type** is the Python type a column decodes to, and the leaf your row type must use.
- **Accepted parameters** are the Python types that can be interpolated into a parameter of that type. `None` (SQL
  NULL) is accepted for every parameter.
- **Encoding** is the wire format used to send a parameter.

| Type key | Result type | Timezone | Accepted parameters | Encoding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bool` | `bool` |  | `bool` | binary |
| `int2` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `int4` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `int8` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `oid` | `int` |  | `int` | binary |
| `float4` | `float` |  | `float`, `int` | binary |
| `float8` | `float` |  | `float`, `int` | binary |
| `numeric` | `decimal.Decimal` |  | `Decimal`, `int` | text |
| `text` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `varchar` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `bpchar` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `name` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `citext` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `char` | `str` |  | `str` | binary |
| `bytea` | `bytes` |  | `bytes`, `bytearray`, `memoryview` | binary |
| `date` | `datetime.date` |  | `date` | binary |
| `time` | `datetime.time` | naive | `time` | binary |
| `timetz` | `datetime.time` | aware | `time` | text |
| `timestamp` | `datetime.datetime` | naive | `datetime` | binary |
| `timestamptz` | `datetime.datetime` | aware | `datetime` | binary |
| `interval` | `datetime.timedelta` |  | `timedelta` | binary |
| `uuid` | `uuid.UUID` |  | `UUID`, `str` | binary |
| `json` | any value (`json.loads`) |  | any JSON-serialisable value | text |
| `jsonb` | any value (`json.loads`) |  | any JSON-serialisable value | text |
| `enum` | `str` |  | `str` | text |
| `domain` | base type |  | base type | base type |
| `array` | `list[X]` |  | `list`, `tuple` | binary, or text if an element needs it |
| `void` | `None` |  | none |  |

## Notes

- `bool` is never accepted for an integer parameter, and `datetime` is never accepted for a `date` parameter.
- A `float4`/`float8` parameter takes an `int`, but an `int` above 2^53 loses precision.
- `str` is never treated as a sequence, so it cannot be bound to an array parameter.
- `json` and `jsonb` accept any JSON-serialisable value, always encoded with `json.dumps`. A `str` becomes a JSON
  string; to bind raw JSON text, write `{s}::text::jsonb`.
- Timezone rules are checked when encoding: a naive `datetime` for `timestamptz` (or an aware one for `timestamp`)
  raises `EncodeError`.
- A domain behaves as its base type.
- An array column decodes to `list[X]` (nested lists for multi-dimensional arrays). `list[X]` and `list[X | None]`
  both match, at every nesting level.
- `void` decodes to `None` and is only valid as a tuple element.
- Any type not listed here is `unsupported-type` in the checker and raises `DecodeError` at runtime (for example
  `money`, `inet`, ranges, composites and `xml`).

## Differences from psycopg

Decoding the same server value with rowx and with psycopg gives equal results, except for these cases. A test asserts
that this list matches the one it checks.

- `timestamptz`: rowx always returns a UTC-aware value, while psycopg uses the session `TimeZone`; the instants are
  equal.
- `float4`: rowx widens the exact 32-bit value to a `float`, while psycopg parses the shortest decimal text; the values
  are equal after rounding to 32 bits.
- `char`: A non-ASCII `"char"` is cut to one byte by the server, which is not valid UTF-8, so rowx raises `DecodeError`.
- `interval`: An interval with a month or year part raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg approximates a month as 30 days.
- `date`: An infinite date raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `timestamp`: An infinite timestamp raises `DecodeError`, while psycopg raises its own `DataError`.
- `void`: `void` decodes to `None`, while psycopg returns an empty string.
